chapter: Childhood in Tyler, Beaumont and Houston
title: Sitting in with the Lincoln Theatre pit band
summary: The six-piece pit band's drummer, Abner Jones, noticing him in the front every day, lets twelve-year-old Gus sit in on the full set.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: I noticed the way she looked at me, and everything was okay. And he told her he was going to take me to the theatre. All right, we went to the theatre. And I went in there and the first thing, I went right down in front. Because the band was there, they had a six-piece band, drums, piano, bass, a violin player, trumpet and a saxophone player.
Yeah. No guitar, no banjo or anything.
No, no guitar or banjo.
Yeah.
But they had a very good violin player.
Yeah.
And the drummer was named Abner Jones.
Oh?
And I used to go and watch him every day --
Was he a good drummer?
-- because I didn't have to pay to go in the theatre.
That was a big break, wasn't it?
Sure was.
Some free schooling.

And so Abner said, 'I see you all the time in here.' He said, 'You just watch all the time. Can you play drums?' I said, 'A little bit.' He said, 'You want to sit in and play?' And when he said that, I got nervous. I said 'Yes,' and so he knew I was --
Do or die.
Yeah, so they played a medium slow number, and I sat there and kept time. And --
On the snare or something.
No, on the whole set, the whole set. He had the whole set.
He got up and you sat down?
I sat down.
Oh, my. And what, you were only about 13 or 14?
I was about 12 years old.
How about that?
